Window cleaning in Melbourne

Window cleaning, including the ones you cannot reach

Glass inside and out, frames, sills and tracks, across single and double storey homes in Melbourne. Upstairs glazing is done from the ground with a water fed pole, so there are no ladders against your render and no access charge on a normal house.

  • Glass, frames, sills and tracks
  • Purified water, no detergent residue
  • Second storey from the ground
Get A Quote 0400 638 010
  1. Home
  2. Services
  3. Windows, gutters, roof and solar
  4. Window cleaning

What a window clean covers

Both faces of the accessible glass, plus the frames, the sills and the tracks. The tracks are the part most people mean when they say the windows never look properly done, because glass over a dirty track dirties itself again the first time a window is opened.

Downstairs is cleaned by hand with a squeegee, which is still the best finish on reachable glass. Upstairs is done from the ground with a water fed pole running purified water. That water has had its minerals stripped out, so it dries without leaving spots and the glass is left to dry rather than wiped. It is also why a pole-cleaned window can look slightly wet when we leave and perfect an hour later.

When glass will not come clean

The things on glass that are not dirt, and what each one means

If your windows look hazy after they have been washed, it is almost certainly one of these rather than a bad clean.

The last column is the honest one. Two of these are permanent and no window cleaner can fix them.
  What it is What it looks like Can it be removed
Hard water spotting Minerals left behind when sprinkler or bore water dries on the glass Round spots or a milky film, worst on the side facing the garden Yes if it is recent. Long standing deposit has usually etched
Construction deposit Render run off, concrete slurry and cutting fines from a build A fine overall haze, often with hard flecks Yes if caught early. This is why new build glazing is cleaned before handover
Etching The glass surface itself eaten into by the above, left too long A permanent cloudiness that does not change when the glass is wet No. Only replacement, and we will tell you rather than keep scrubbing
Failed double glazing The seal between the panes has gone and moisture is inside the unit Fogging or condensation between two panes that cannot be wiped No. It is a glazier's job, not a cleaner's
Paint and silicone Overspray, splashes or smeared sealant from a trade Discrete specks or films in one area rather than overall Usually yes, by blade and solvent, carefully and at your direction
Pool chemistry on balustrades Chlorinated splash drying repeatedly on the same glass A dull band at splash height on frameless panels Usually yes, and then it needs a sealer or it returns

Swipe for the rest of the columns

Scope

What is in a standard window clean

Included

On every residential window clean.

  • Exterior glass on all accessible windows and glazed doors
  • Interior glass where rooms are accessible and furniture allows
  • Frames wiped down, including the rebate the sash sits in
  • Sills cleaned, not just the glass above them
  • Tracks vacuumed and wiped, which is what stops them dirtying the glass again
  • Flyscreens removed, brushed off and refitted
  • Cobwebs cleared from the frames and the surrounds

Not included, or quoted separately

Some of these are add ons, some are another trade.

  • Internal glass where access needs furniture moved. Tell us and we will plan for it
  • Skylights and roof glazing, which need roof access
  • Glass balustrades and pool glass, which have their own page
  • Commercial shopfronts and offices, which are scheduled work
  • Multi storey buildings, which need specialist access
  • Replacing or repairing flyscreens, which we will point out but do not fix
  • Removing paint or silicone, which we will do at your direction but not by default

Why the upstairs glass is done from the ground

A water fed pole is a telescopic carbon fibre pole with a brush head and a water line running up the inside. The water has been through a filter that strips the dissolved minerals out of it, which is the whole trick: with nothing dissolved in it, the water dries off the glass leaving nothing behind.

The brush agitates, the water rinses, and the glass is left wet. No squeegee, no cloth, no one standing on a ladder leaning against your render with a bucket. It is safer, it is faster, and it reaches the frames and the top of the glass properly rather than as far as someone can stretch.

What it will not do

A pole cannot remove something bonded to the glass. Hard water deposit, paint and construction film need hand work with a blade or a chemical, which means reaching the glass. On a second storey that may mean a ladder or, rarely, a platform, and we will tell you that before the day rather than quietly leaving it.

Downstairs we hand clean regardless, because a squeegee on reachable glass still gives the best finish anyone has found.

How often

What the honest interval is for a Melbourne house

STEP 01

Twice a year

The default for most homes. Once before summer and once after winter catches the two things that dirty glass most: the spring pollen and growth, and the winter grime and spotting.

STEP 02

Every three months

Worth it on a main road, near a construction site, close to the coast, or where sprinklers hit the glass. In those situations deposit builds fast enough that leaving it longer risks etching.

STEP 03

Once a year

Fine for a sheltered house set back from traffic with no sprinklers near the windows. More than that is not buying you much.

STEP 04

When it matters

Before a party, a photographer, an inspection or a sale campaign. Glass is one of the cheapest things on a property to make look new.

What moves the price

Priced per property, not per pane

How much glass, not how many windows

A house with four large stacker doors has more glass than one with twelve small windows, and takes longer. Counting windows is a poor guide and we do not quote that way.

Single or double storey

Upstairs glazing needs the pole set up. It is not expensive, but it is a real part of the time on site.

Inside as well as out

Interior glass roughly doubles the time, because of access, furniture and working around people. Plenty of people have the outside done more often than the inside.

Condition and interval

A first clean on glass that has not been touched in three years is a different job from the second one six months later. Regular cleans are cheaper per visit for exactly that reason.

Tracks, screens and sills

Included as standard here, but worth knowing that this is where other quotes differ. A cheaper price that is glass only is not the same job.

Access around the house

A clear path around the perimeter makes it quick. A deck, a pool fence, a narrow side gate or a dog changes how long it takes.

Often booked together

What people add to a window clean

Gutter cleaning

The obvious pairing: the gear is already out and the ladder is already up.

Frameless panels, which mark differently because of pool chemistry.

Walls first, then glass. Doing it the other way round just dirties the windows again.

Questions

Asked before booking a window clean

How is window cleaning priced?

Per pane or per property, and which one suits you depends entirely on how many panes your house has. A modern home with large fixed panels does well out of a per pane price. A period home with glazing bars does not.

What window cleaning costs in Melbourne explains both models and what the extras usually are.

How much does window cleaning cost in Melbourne?

It is priced on the property rather than per window: how much glass there is, whether it is single or double storey, and whether you want the inside done as well. A standard single storey home outside only is the cheapest end. A double storey with large stacker doors, inside and out, is the other.

Tell us the suburb, the number of storeys and roughly how much glazing, and you will get a fixed price without anyone coming out.

Do you clean the tracks and flyscreens too?

Yes, both, as standard. Tracks are vacuumed and wiped, and flyscreens are taken out, brushed down and put back. This is the main thing to check when you are comparing quotes, because a lower price that covers glass only is not the same job and the glass will not stay clean over a dirty track.

Do I need to be home?

For an exterior clean, no, as long as we can get around the house and there is an outside tap. For interior work someone needs to let us in, and it helps if blinds are up and anything fragile is off the sills.

How do you reach second storey windows without ladders?

A water fed pole: a telescopic pole with a brush head and purified water running through it. It reaches the second storey comfortably from the ground, it cleans the frames as well as the glass, and nothing leans against your render.

Where something is bonded to the upstairs glass and needs hand work, we will tell you what access that needs and what it costs before the day.

Why do the windows look wet and streaky when you leave?

Because pole cleaned glass is deliberately left to dry rather than wiped. The water has had its minerals stripped out, so it dries off clean and leaves nothing behind. Give it an hour. If anything is still marked after that, tell us and we will come back.

Can you clean windows in the rain?

Yes, which surprises people. Rain is clean water. What dirties glass is the deposit the rain washes down from a dirty frame, so cleaning the frames is what stops it. We avoid heavy rain for the sake of the interior work and for safety, but light rain is not a reason to reschedule.

What about hard water spots that will not come off?

Recent spotting comes off with the right treatment. Long standing deposit has usually etched the glass, and at that point no amount of cleaning brings it back because the surface itself is damaged. We will tell you which one you have rather than charging you to find out.

The fix is the sprinkler, not the glass. Once it is clean, keeping bore and sprinkler water off the windows is what stops it recurring.
